hashed.why: THE HOUSE RULES THEMSELVES, and they live outside src/+tests/ so no walk of the discovery roots reaches them. Break FSHW-CLAIM-001 or delete a rule and, before this was declared, a green earned while the rule held still reported Applies. The directory is declared rather than a glob so the .fsproj is covered too: the compile list decides which rules are in the assembly at all.
The per-file coverage floors. Lower one and a verdict earned under the higher floor must stop applying; hashing it is the only thing that makes that true.
The coverage collector's include/exclude filters. Widen an exclusion and files stop being measured at all, which moves every floor beneath it without touching the floors file.
The lint rules the lint plugin enforces. Disabling one changes what the check concludes about an unchanged tree.
The restore-only project that materializes the FSharpLint analyzer the check loads. Move its pin and a different set of findings is produced from the same source.

notInputs.reason: Release prose. No plugin reads it, so it cannot change what a check concludes — and re-earning a full unfiltered verdict for a paragraph about work that was already gated buys nothing. Stated here rather than merely absent, so the exclusion is reviewable instead of invisible. This declaration RECORDS that decision; it does not perform it. `notInputs` is parsed and validated but read by neither TreeHash nor Discovery, so nothing here subtracts a file from the hash — deliberately, since a config able to do that would be a supported way to weaken the gate. What actually keeps this file out is that the walk covers src/ and tests/ only, and the repo root is not in it. NOTE the per-package CHANGELOGs under src/ ARE hashed: they are inside the discovery roots, and carving holes in that walk is a bigger hazard than the re-gate.
Configures the RELEASE tagger, which runs after a verdict is earned and never contributes to one. Changing it changes what gets published, not what the check concludes.

excluded.reason: 67 END-TO-END tests (IntegrationTests 58, PluginTimeout 2, PluginActivityConcurrency 2, NuGetToolBarrierOracle 3, TestPruneStorm 1, ProcessHelperTimeout 1) that stand up REAL infrastructure — live plugin hosts and daemons over temp repos, real file watchers, real child `dotnet` processes — and assert on WALL-CLOCK behaviour: plugin timeouts, process reaping, activity concurrency, TestPrune under a storm of edits. Run from inside the daemon that IS the gate, they nest a daemon in a daemon and contend for the box the outer run is being timed on, so their timing assertions become a function of machine load rather than of the code. Their coverage is excluded for the same family of reasons (no Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage reference: SDK-reflection paths fire nondeterministically and would make the ratchet flaky — see CLAUDE.md). NOT UNGATED: `mise run test-integration` runs them, and CI's reusable workflow runs a solution-wide `dotnet test` that includes them, so they must be green to merge — just not from inside the warm-daemon inner loop. The exclusion is DECLARED: it is logged on every green load and recorded in verdict.json's `scope.excluded`, so a consumer of a `kind: full` verdict sees the gap instead of inferring completeness from a count.

A one-test xUnit v4 runner FIXTURE, not a suite. FsHotWatch.Tests builds it through a project reference and drives it through the real xUnit v4 runner and CTRF harness (TestPruneRunnerFamilyTests), so its runner behaviour is verified by the configured suite. Declared here because daemon discovery indexes its test methods: without a reasoned exclusion, any change to its own symbols would stay owed to a project the gate never runs.
